provenance.note: A case that clearly violates CW assumptions: a chaser offset radially by 1,000 km from a 6,778 km circular reference radius (~14.8% separation ratio -- well beyond local relative-motion proximity, not a few hundred meters). It is explicitly declared as a coast-only point-mass request (no targeting, no burns), so it fits the bounded two-body fallback contract (src/twobody.py) exactly, and src/model_selector.py routes it there rather than to CW.

request.natural_language: A spacecraft is in Earth orbit with an initial inertial Cartesian state position [7778000, 0, 0] m, velocity [0, 7158.7124559338245, 0] m/s. Earth's gravitational parameter is 398600441800000.0 m^3/s^2. Propagate this state forward 900 seconds under point-mass gravity only (no thrust, no perturbations, no targeting). Report the final inertial Cartesian state.

expected_structured_problem._comment: This request is declared coast-only, inertial-Cartesian, and explicitly outside the two-spacecraft LVLH-relative rendezvous class the orbital-problem-formalizer skill supports (it is a single-spacecraft propagation request). Per that skill, it is labeled 'out of scope' for the formalizer rather than coerced into the LVLH rendezvous schema; the case instead proceeds directly to the bounded two-body coast contract (.pi/skills/orbital-two-body-rendezvous/SKILL.md), which is the correct downstream handling per reference/SOURCE.md Sec C.

scope.reason: Single-spacecraft inertial-Cartesian coast propagation request, not a two-spacecraft LVLH-relative rendezvous; routed instead to the bounded two-body coast contract (src/twobody.py), per .pi/skills/orbital-two-body-rendezvous/SKILL.md.

circularity.value: not applicable (inertial Cartesian state given directly)

requested_outputs.value: final inertial Cartesian state after coast

blocking_issues: Request is a single-spacecraft inertial coast propagation, outside the two-spacecraft LVLH-relative rendezvous class the formalizer schema supports.

expected_model._comment: Per src/model_selector.py: circularity/frame/other required items are supplied, but locality and other_physics are VIOLATED (the separation is not local relative motion, and a 1,000 km radial offset at this altitude is not negligible-perturbation small-relative-velocity CW geometry). The case independently satisfies the bounded two-body coast contract (finite 6-element inertial state, positive mu, finite duration, positive RK4 step count, coast-only), so it routes to the bounded two-body fallback rather than UNSUPPORTED.

must_state: coast-only; no targeting, maneuvers, or optimization claimed
must_not_state: a solved rendezvous or executed maneuver
